Signature Dishes

No long menu, no fuss — just the handful of items this house is known for, grilled fresh over charcoal the old way.

Reshmi Boti

The house favourite — soft, creamy-marinated boti that melts in the mouth, lightly charred at the edges and served sizzling off the skewer.

House Favourite

Beef Kebab

Hand-shaped beef seekh kebabs, spiced the traditional way and grilled until juicy inside with a proper smoky crust outside.

Charcoal Grilled

Champ (Ribs)

Tender ribs grilled low and slow over the coals — rich, sticky and full of that deep BBQ flavour old Lahore swears by.

Slow Grilled

BBQ, The Old Way

Everything here is cooked on a traditional open charcoal grill — no shortcuts. The smoke, the sizzle and the spice are the whole recipe.

Open Charcoal Grill

Ninety-plus years inside Mochi Gate

Pak Punjab Tikka House claims an establishment dating back to 1930 — from a time when the Walled City was the beating heart of Lahore, and a good tikka was judged by the crowd standing around the grill.

The shop stands at Lal Khoo, inside Mochi Gate — one of the thirteen gates of the old city — where narrow streets, centuries-old havelis and the smell of charcoal smoke have gone together for as long as anyone can remember.

Through it all, the formula never changed: fresh meat, honest spices, live coals, and food served the moment it leaves the skewer.

  • 1930

    Claimed founding of the house inside Mochi Gate, Walled City.

  • Today

    A rooftop for open-air seating and a family hall opposite the shop, still grilling at Lal Khoo.

Come Hungry, Stay Late

An old-city evening done properly — dinner under the open sky, with the whole family.

Rooftop Seating

Take your BBQ up to the rooftop and eat with a view over the rooftops and lanes of the old Walled City — at its best after sunset, when the grill is at its busiest.

Family Hall

Bringing the whole family? A family hall sits right opposite the shop, so everyone can sit comfortably and enjoy the same food fresh off the coals.

Opening Hours

Open daily, afternoon till late night. Evenings are the liveliest time at Lal Khoo — arrive hungry and expect the grill to be in full swing.

Loved Across Lahore

Decades in the Walled City have earned this little shop a big reputation.
